title: Substructures in the Disk-forming Region of the Class 0 Low-mass Protostellar Source IRAS 16293-2422 Source A on a 10 au Scale
question: What are the substructures, kinematic structures, and gas-temperature distribution in the disk-forming region of the Class 0 protostellar source IRAS 16293-2422 Source A on a 10 au scale?

data.sensitivity: 0.3 mJy/beam (Briggs continuum), 0.2 mJy/beam (uniform continuum), 2.5 mJy/beam (C17O at 0.2 km/s), 2.0 mJy/beam (H2CS at 0.2 km/s), 1.1 mJy/beam (C17O at 1 km/s), 0.9 mJy/beam (H2CS at 1 km/s)

what.value: VLA 2 cm (15 GHz) and 0.9 cm (33 GHz) continuum images and proper motions of continuum peaks

evidence.loc: 3.1. 1.3 mm Continuum
evidence.quote: More clumpy features of Source A has recently been reported in the 2 cm (15 GHz) and 0.9 cm (33 GHz) continuum images observed with VLA by Hern´andez-G´omez et al. (2019).

evidence.loc: Figure 2 caption
evidence.quote: (a, b) The continuum images at 15 GHz (a; contour) and 33 GHz (b; contour) reported by Hern´andez-G´omez et al. (2019) overlaid on the 1.3 mm continuum image (color).

what.value: Spectral line parameters from JPL and CDMS databases

evidence.loc: 4.4.1. Rotating Disk around A1
evidence.quote: Note that this line is free from significant contamination lines by other lines according to the spectral line database (JPL and CDMS; Pickett et al. 1998; M¨uller et al. 2005; Endres et al. 2016)

external_data.citation: Pickett et al. 1998; Müller et al. 2005; Endres et al. 2016

recipe.goal: Identify continuum substructures and measure peak positions and intensities
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fitting on 1.3 mm continuum images (Briggs robust=0.5 and uniform weighting) using the 2D Fit Tool of casa viewer, and comparison with extrapolated VLA proper motions
key_parameters: Briggs robust = 0.5 and uniform (robust = -2.0) continuum maps

recipe.goal: Determine morphological parameters of the circummultiple disk/envelope system
recipe.method: Calculate the intensity centroid of 1.3 mm continuum data points above 3 sigma (0.9 mJy/beam) and fit those positions to an ellipse using intensity-weighted least-squares
assumptions: Flat disk structure without thickness for inclination angle lower limit; dust emission intensity proportional to dust mass

recipe.goal: Model the kinematic structure of the circummultiple structure using C17O (J=2-1)
recipe.method: Extract PV diagrams centered on the continuum intensity centroid and fit 3D Keplerian disk and infalling-rotating envelope (IRE) models using reduced chi-squared tests on the blue-shifted component
key_parameters: Inner radius = 50 au (or r_CB = 50 au), outer radius = 300 au, P.A. = 50 deg, V_sys = 3.9 km/s, flared angle = 30 deg, intrinsic FWHM = 1 km/s, emissivity proportional to r^-1.5
assumptions: Optically thin line emission, no radiative transfer, ballistic motion conserving energy and specific angular momentum for IRE model

recipe.goal: Model the kinematic structure of the circumstellar disk around protostar A1 using H2CS
recipe.method: Extract PV diagrams centered on continuum peak A1 and fit 3D Keplerian disk and infalling-rotating envelope models to H2CS (7_4,3-6_4,2, 7_4,4-6_4,3) along P.A. 50 deg and 140 deg using reduced chi-squared tests
key_parameters: V_sys = 2.5 km/s, outer radius = 30 au, inner radius = 0.56 au (1 pixel) for Keplerian or r_CB = 5, 10, 20 au for IRE, P.A. = 50 deg, flared angle = 30 deg, intrinsic FWHM = 1 km/s, emissivity proportional to r^-1.5
assumptions: Optically thin line emission, center of gravity at continuum peak A1

recipe.goal: Derive the H2CS rotation temperature distribution and line-of-sight maximum temperature profile
recipe.method: Calculate the intensity ratio of H2CS (7_4,3-6_4,2, 7_4,4-6_4,3) to H2CS (7_2,5-6_2,4) from integrated intensity maps, 1 km/s velocity channel maps, and peak along the velocity axis (using CASA immoments moments=[8]), and convert to rotation temperature
key_parameters: High-temperature limit of intensity ratio = 1.47 for T = infinity; rms noise = 6 mJy/beam km/s (integrated) and 2 mJy/beam (cube)
assumptions: LTE condition and optically thin emission for both H2CS lines; dust continuum contribution ignored
